parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
An ideal battery of emf ε is connected to resistor R1, followed by two parallel branches. One branch contains R2; the other contains R3 and R4 in series. Each resistor has resistance R.

Derive the currents through R1 and R3 in terms of ε and R.

answer.text: The parallel combination is R × 2R/(R + 2R) = 2R/3. The total resistance is 5R/3, so I1 = 3ε/(5R). The parallel-section voltage is 2ε/5, giving I3 = (2ε/5)/(2R) = ε/(5R).

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
An ideal battery of emf ε is connected to resistor R1, followed by two parallel branches. One branch contains R2; the other contains R3 and R4 in series. Each resistor has resistance R.

Express the potential difference across each resistor as a fraction of ε.

answer.text: VR1 = 3ε/5; VR2 = 2ε/5; VR3 = ε/5; VR4 = ε/5. The voltage across R2 equals the combined voltage across R3 and R4.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
An ideal battery of emf ε is connected to resistor R1, followed by two parallel branches. One branch contains R2; the other contains R3 and R4 in series. Each resistor has resistance R.

A student claims the total power dissipated is 3ε²/(5R). Assess the claim, showing your reasoning.

answer.text: The claim is correct. Req = R + (R × 2R)/(R + 2R) = 5R/3. Hence P = ε²/Req = 3ε²/(5R).

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
An ideal battery of emf ε is connected to resistor R1, followed by two parallel branches. One branch contains R2; the other contains R3 and R4 in series. Each resistor has resistance R.

The battery is replaced by one of the same emf but nonzero internal resistance r. Explain whether the power dissipated in R1 increases, decreases or stays the same.

answer.text: It decreases. The total circuit resistance becomes 5R/3 + r, so the current through R1 decreases. Since R is unchanged, PR1 = I1²R decreases.
